title: UIBC key revocation list report line
description: One line of a JSON Lines file produced by `uibc_core.pyz verify-key-revocation-list --report`. It answers one question — is this key revoked at this time — and carries the rule that produced the answer, because `rejected` here can mean four different things and a bare decision hands the reader nothing to check. The decision maps onto the suite's external-verifier contract: 0 revoked, 1 not revoked, 2 no statement, 3 rejected, 4 stale.

vector.description: The corpus member (one case directory) this line is about.

result.description: PASS for revoked, not_revoked and no_statement — the three answers the suite treats as reached; FAIL for rejected and stale; ERROR when the case could not be read. PASS here is a conforming answer, not an approval of the key.

decision.description: null only on an ERROR line. `no_statement` means the list does not cover this key: it is not `not_revoked`.

reason.description: One of the suite's nine tokens: signer_not_trusted, list_signature_invalid, list_older_than_accepted, list_stale, revoked_in_list, revoked_kept_from_earlier_list, revocation_not_yet_effective, key_not_covered, covered_no_entry.

basis.description: The rule that produced the decision, with whatever facts it rested on: {"rule": "trusted_by_recomputed_thumbprint" | "signature" | "freshness" | "in_list" | "retained" | "absent" | "shape", ...}. Null only on an ERROR line.

exit.description: The suite's contract: the process exits by the decision. 3 is reached both by `rejected` and by an unreadable case; the `result` field tells them apart.

error.description: Present only on an ERROR line, and required there.

$comment: Cross-field rules the subset here cannot express: exit equals the decision's code (revoked 0, not_revoked 1, no_statement 2, rejected 3, stale 4); result is FAIL only for rejected and stale; an ERROR line carries null decision, null reason, null basis and an error string.
